breaking_changes: The FastFlowLM NPU model hy-mt2:1.8b was renamed to hy-mt2-flash:1.8b in the upstream v1.0.7 release; update any configs or scripts that reference the old hy-mt2:1.8b tag.

checklist.author: @fl0rianr
checklist.text: Register a model whose files are only in --extra-models-dir, then attempt DELETE /api/v1/delete; confirm the model registration is removed but the GGUF file on disk is preserved.

checklist.author: @bitgamma
checklist.text: Start the Lemonade server on a Windows system with an AMD ROCm GPU, set the thenoise backend to rocm, and generate an image to confirm the bundled Python interpreter launches and produces output.

checklist.author: @ramkrishna2910
checklist.text: On Windows, connect to a server using an internal or private CA certificate (not a public CA like Let's Encrypt) and confirm the HTTPS connection succeeds without SSL connect errors.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Start the server on macOS with extra_models_dir set to a directory containing nested subfolders, write a model file into one subfolder, and confirm the server's model list updates within a few seconds without any external trigger.

checklist.author: @julianxhokaxhiu
checklist.text: On a machine with an NPU, install this release and confirm that lemonade can discover and serve the hy-mt2-flash:1.8b model by name.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Start the server, configure a very long global_timeout, and download a large model from a slow or flaky endpoint to confirm the download does not abort prematurely at 60 seconds but respects the global_timeout value.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Start the server with extra_models_dir pointing at a Hugging Face cache that has two snapshots, set refs/main to the first, confirm the model lists as <repo> and <repo>-<quant>, then rename refs/main to the second snapshot and confirm the model name <repo> now resolves to the new checkpoint while the old snapshot is listed as <old-commit>-<repo>.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Set extra_models_dir to a Hugging Face cache with two different orgs shipping the same repo name, confirm the first org's models list as <repo> and the second's as <org>-<repo>, then swap the directory listing order and confirm the names stay the same (org qualification, not discovery order).

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Set extra_models_dir to a cache whose GGUFs are in a subfolder like Q4_K_M/, confirm the model name is <repo>-Q4_K_M, then request that model by name to confirm it loads correctly.

checklist.author: @github-actions[bot]
checklist.text: Start the server with vulkan, rocm-stable, or rocm-nightly backend and load one model using each new architecture (clef, glm5-next, hrm_text, hy_v4, maple, spark2_5) to confirm it loads and answers without error.

checklist.author: @fl0rianr
checklist.text: Start lemond with a registered GGUF model (e.g. LFM2.5-8B-A1B) whose HF cache is copied into --extra-models-dir, then confirm the model appears under its original catalog name (not extra.*) in the /models API response.

checklist.author: @fl0rianr
checklist.text: Start lemond with --extra-models-dir containing a complete repo with a main GGUF, an MTP companion, and a DFlash.gguf file; confirm only the main GGUF appears as a model and the companions do not create separate entries.

checklist.author: @fl0rianr
checklist.text: Register a model with a sharded GGUF (e.g. Shards-Q4_K_M-00001-of-00002.gguf) whose complete shard family and other quantizations exist in --extra-models-dir; confirm only the unrelated quantizations appear as extra.* models, not the registered shards.

checklist.author: @fl0rianr
checklist.text: Set --extra-models-dir with a refs/main entry that is a symlink to a sibling repository cache; confirm the model is NOT adopted from the sibling and remains un-downloaded.

checklist.author: @fl0rianr
checklist.text: Register a user model with an mmproj auxiliary checkpoint and place both files in --extra-models-dir under a legacy multi-repo layout (auxiliary in the main repo cache); confirm the model retains its registration and can still be deleted via the API without error.

checklist.author: @fl0rianr
checklist.text: Start lemond with a non-GGUF catalog model (e.g. Krea-2-Turbo) whose multi-file cache is in --extra-models-dir; confirm the model loads with its original recipe (thenoise) and is not listed in the extra models endpoint.

checklist.author: @julianxhokaxhiu
checklist.text: Verify that any existing model registrations using the old hy-mt2:1.8b tag fail gracefully or produce a clear error, since the upstream binary no longer recognises that identifier.

evidence.blockers: No blockers. The release candidate has comprehensive CI coverage across all platforms, with two commits requiring manual verification on specific platforms — Windows ROCm for TheNoise and Windows internal CA for HTTPS connections.
evidence.breaking_changes: One breaking change: the upstream FastFlowLM v1.0.7 renamed the hy-mt2:1.8b model tag to hy-mt2-flash:1.8b. Users referencing the old tag must update their configs. The rename is a straightforward string replacement with no migration script needed.
evidence.coverage: Every commit in the release range from v2026.41.1 to the release candidate was reviewed across all platforms. The range includes backend version bumps, model discovery fixes, CLI improvements, and documentation updates.
evidence.manual_testing: Manual verification is needed on Windows with AMD ROCm GPU for TheNoise backend, on Windows with internal or private CA certificates for HTTPS connections, on macOS for nested extra_models_dir FSEvents watching, on NPU hardware for the renamed hy-mt2-flash model, and on a large model download from a slow endpoint for timeout behavior.
evidence.security: One security-relevant change: Windows TLS now uses CURLSSLOPT_REVOKE_BEST_EFFORT, which relaxes revocation checking when CRL/OCSP responders are unavailable. This enables connections to servers with internal CAs but introduces a low risk of accepting revoked certificates from private CAs without revocation infrastructure. The change is scoped to Windows and only activates when responders are unreachable.
